paragraphs.title: The King’s Joy and Fulfilled Requests

easy.explanation: The king rejoices in the LORD’s strength and salvation.
easy.q: In what does the king rejoice?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “in thy salvation,” addressing the LORD.
easy.q: To whom is salvation attributed in these verses?

easy.explanation: The psalm says, “Thou hast given him his heart’s desire.”
easy.q: What did the LORD give the king?

answers: The salvation causes the king to rejoice greatly
The salvation causes the king to be afraid
The salvation prevents the king from asking
medium.explanation: The king rejoices greatly in the LORD’s salvation.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the LORD’s salvation and the king’s joy?

medium.explanation: The phrase refers to the request the king expressed with his lips.
medium.q: What does “the request of his lips” refer to?

answers: The LORD answered both his inward desire and expressed prayer
The king rejoiced only because of his enemies
medium.explanation: The verses mention both the king’s inward desire and his spoken request.
medium.q: What does the combination of “his heart’s desire” and “the request of his lips” show?

answers: The king credits the LORD with both power and deliverance
The king trusts only in his own strength
The king does not need salvation
challenge.explanation: The king’s joy recognizes both the LORD’s strength and the salvation He gives.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the king rejoicing in both the LORD’s strength and salvation?

answers: The king’s joy, his desire being given, and his request being answered
A crown, length of days, and victory
challenge.explanation: The first three verses move from rejoicing to answered desire and prayer.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the opening of the psalm?

challenge.explanation: The phrase describes abundant or extraordinary rejoicing.
challenge.q: What does “how greatly shall he rejoice” indicate about the king’s joy?

paragraphs.title: Blessings, Life, and Honor for the King

easy.explanation: The LORD set “a crown of pure gold” on his head.
easy.q: What did the LORD set on the king’s head?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “He asked life of thee.”
easy.q: What did the king ask of the LORD?

easy.explanation: The psalm says, “the king trusteth in the LORD.”
easy.q: In whom does the king trust?

answers: Length of days for ever and ever
medium.explanation: The LORD gives him “length of days for ever and ever.”
medium.q: What does the LORD give the king besides life?

answers: The LORD removed honor from him
The LORD placed honor and splendor upon him
medium.explanation: The statement says that the LORD bestowed honor and majesty upon the king.
medium.q: What does “honour and majesty hast thou laid upon him” mean?

answers: Because he trusts in the LORD and His mercy
medium.explanation: His trust in the LORD and the mercy of the Most High keeps him steadfast.
medium.q: Why will the king not be moved?

answers: Blessings, crown, life, honor, and gladness
challenge.explanation: The passage mentions blessings, a golden crown, life, honor, and great gladness.
challenge.q: Which order of blessings appears in these verses?

answers: Trusting the LORD means the king shall not be moved
Trust causes the king to give up his life
Trust prevents him from receiving blessings
challenge.explanation: The verse connects the king’s trust in the LORD with his not being moved.
challenge.q: What is the connection between trusting the LORD and the king’s stability?

answers: The blessing is given to the enemies
The blessing is lasting and enduring
challenge.explanation: The words “for ever” emphasize the continuing nature of the blessing.
challenge.q: What does “most blessed for ever” emphasize?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Thine hand shall find out all thine enemies.”
easy.q: Whom shall the king’s hand find?

easy.explanation: The enemies are compared to “a fiery oven.”
easy.q: What image is used to describe the enemies?

answers: It will be destroyed from the earth
easy.explanation: The psalm says, “Their fruit shalt thou destroy from the earth.”
easy.q: What will happen to the enemies’ fruit?

answers: They will not be able to perform them
medium.explanation: They imagined a device, but were not able to perform it.
medium.q: What will happen to the enemies’ intended plans?

medium.explanation: A mischievous device is a harmful or evil plan.
medium.q: What does “a mischievous device” mean in this context?

answers: The LORD swallows them in wrath, and fire devours them
medium.explanation: The verse describes the LORD swallowing them in wrath and fire devouring them.
medium.q: How is judgment against the enemies described?

answers: The reach and power of the king against his enemies
challenge.explanation: The hand and right hand represent power reaching and overcoming the enemies.
challenge.q: What do “thine hand” and “thy right hand” communicate in the description of victory?

answers: A successful plan, blessing, and life
Their discovery, destruction by fire, and loss of fruit and seed
Singing, a crown, and length of days
challenge.explanation: The passage describes their defeat, destruction, and the removal of their future descendants.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the enemies’ fate?

answers: An evil intention alone does not guarantee success
The enemies did not think at all
challenge.explanation: They intended evil, but their plan could not be carried out.
challenge.q: What can be understood from the enemies intending evil but being unable to perform it?

easy.explanation: The verse addresses the LORD: “Be thou exalted, LORD.”
easy.q: To whom is the command “Be thou exalted” addressed?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “so will we sing and praise thy power.”
easy.q: What will the speakers do because of the LORD’s strength?

easy.explanation: The speakers will sing and praise the LORD’s power.
easy.q: What is the subject of the song at the end of the psalm?

answers: Be lifted up or revealed in greatness
medium.explanation: The phrase calls for the LORD to be lifted up and displayed in His greatness.
medium.q: What does “Be thou exalted” mean in this verse?

answers: The LORD’s power is the reason for singing and praise
The singing is intended for the enemies
medium.explanation: The LORD’s power leads the speakers to sing and praise.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the LORD’s strength and singing?

medium.explanation: The final line says, “so will we sing and praise thy power.”
medium.q: Which words describe the response to the LORD’s power?

answers: It turns the descriptions of salvation and victory into praise
It cancels the description of the LORD’s power
It changes to a description of the enemies’ lives
challenge.explanation: After describing the LORD’s help and victory, the psalm ends in praise.
challenge.q: How does the ending connect with the earlier ideas in the psalm?

answers: Sing and praise the LORD’s power
Ask for a crown for the king
challenge.explanation: They declare that they will sing and praise the LORD’s power.
challenge.q: What do the speakers say they will do?

answers: The focus moves from the enemies’ defeat to praise of the LORD
The focus moves from blessings to length of days
The focus moves from prayer to a crown
challenge.explanation: The conclusion shifts from the LORD’s judgment on enemies to worship and praise.
challenge.q: What major change of emphasis occurs in the final verse?
